info.title: LaserData Cloud Core API
info.description:
Control plane: tenants, divisions, environments, deployments, billing, members.

Public REST API for the LaserData Cloud control plane.

## Authentication

Every tenant endpoint accepts either of two auth methods. Pick whichever the Try-It panel shows; both work.
- **API key** (machine / CI / SDK): send in the `ld-api-key` header. Keys are tenant-scoped and bound to a single role. Per-environment scoping is enforced by the role's permissions. Cannot be used on `/account/*` (user-scope) endpoints, tenant creation, leave / delete tenant, or invitation accept / reject.
- **Session cookie** (browser / console): obtained from `POST /account/sign_in`. Mutating endpoints additionally require the `x-csrf-token` header echoed from the sign-in response.

User-scope endpoints (anything under `/account/*`, tenant creation, leave / delete tenant, invitation accept / reject) are session-only and reject API keys with `403 api_key_not_allowed`.

## Idempotency

`POST`, `PUT`, and `PATCH` requests authenticated by an API key may include an `idempotency-key: <opaque>` header (max 255 characters, UUIDv4 recommended). The server caches the first response for 10 minutes per `(api_key, key)` pair and replays it on retries. A reuse with a *different* request body returns `409 idempotency_error`. A reuse while the original request is still in flight returns `409 idempotent_request_in_progress`. Replays carry an `idempotent-replayed: true` header. DELETE is omitted because it is natively idempotent.

## Pagination

List endpoints return a `Paged<T>` body (`page`, `total_pages`, `total_results`, `items`) and a `link` header (RFC 8288) with `rel="first"`, `"prev"`, `"next"`, `"last"` when applicable.

## Errors

Error responses follow RFC 7807 `application/problem+json` with `type`, `title`, `code`, `reason`, `instance`, `status`, `retryable`, and optional `field` / `field_issues`. `retryable` is `true` for 408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504. On 429 or 503 a `retry-after` header may be set in seconds. Otherwise fall back to exponential backoff.

## Response headers

- `ld-request`: request ID. Include it when reporting issues.
- `ld-tenant`, `ld-division`, `ld-environment`, `ld-deployment`, `ld-role`: created-resource ID headers returned on the corresponding `POST` endpoints.
- `link`: pagination relations.
- `retry-after`: wait hint on 429 / 503.
- `idempotent-replayed`: set to `true` when the body is a cached idempotent replay.

get.description: Returns the current user's full account: profile, settings, linked identity providers, and tenant memberships with per-tenant role and permission summary.

Identity-provider callback (Google, GitHub, Microsoft). The IdP redirects the user agent here with ID+token query params. Server resolves the intent and redirects back to the frontend with `intent` (sign_in / sign_up / link_account) appended. Not called directly by API clients.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Intent ID from the IdP redirect

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Intent token from the IdP redirect

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: When present, treated as sign-in flow. Otherwise resolved to sign_up or link_account based on whether the email already belongs to a registered user

307.description: Redirect to the configured frontend with auth intent parameters

500.description: Missing id/token, invalid intent, or IdP failure

post.description: Step 1 of the OAuth sign-in / sign-up flow. Creates a one-time intent and returns the IdP authorization URL the user agent should be redirected to. Source defaults to `google`.

requestBody.description: Identity source selector

200.description: Intent created. The redirect URL points at the IdP authorize endpoint

400.description: Identity source disabled

get.description: Returns a single JSON document with all personal data held about the current user: profile, identities, sessions, memberships, invitations, settings. Use this to satisfy GDPR data-portability requests.

200.description: GDPR data export for the current user

get.description: Returns pending invitations addressed to the current user. Use to populate the console's invitation inbox. Session-only: API keys are tenant-scoped and cannot list user invitations.

put.description: Accepts an invitation and creates the tenant membership. The user immediately has access according to the invitation's role assignment. Session-only: API keys are tenant-scoped and cannot accept user invitations.
Declines an invitation. No membership is created. The inviter is notified. Session-only: API keys are tenant-scoped and cannot reject user invitations.

post.description: Links another identity provider (Google / GitHub / Microsoft) to the current user. Requires a fresh IdP intent for the source being linked. After linking the user can sign in via either provider.

requestBody.description: Intent ID + token for the IdP being linked

200.description: Account linked. Includes a new session when the intent was verified.

409.description: External account already linked to another user

get.description: Lists all active sessions for the current user (one entry per browser/device).

post.description: Extends the current session's expiry. Returns a new session cookie + csrf_token.

delete.description: Signs out the current user everywhere by invalidating every active session. Use this after a suspected credential leak.

put.description: Updates the current user's preferences: default tenant + division (for console nav), theme, and IP binding. IP binding pins active sessions to the IP that created them. Useful for tighter security but breaks roaming.

requestBody.description: Partial update. Null or missing fields are unchanged

400.description: Invalid theme or tenant/division reference

post.description: Step 3 of the OAuth flow. Trades the intent ID+token (received from the IdP callback) for an authenticated session. Sets the `session` cookie and returns a `csrf_token` that must be sent on all subsequent state-changing requests via `x-csrf-token` header.

requestBody.description: Intent ID + token consumed from the IdP callback

200.description: Authenticated session. The csrf_token must be echoed back as X-CSRF-Token on writes

delete.description: Terminates the current session, deletes the session cookie, and invalidates the CSRF token. Subsequent requests must obtain a new session via /account/auth/intents → IdP → /account/sign_in.

post.description: Create a new user account from a verified IdP intent. Optionally provisions a tenant + division (e.g. for SaaS onboarding) or accepts an invitation token. If the IdP-provided email matches an existing tenant's claimed email domain and join_policy allows, the new user joins automatically and a session is returned. Otherwise the account is created in `awaiting_verification` state.

requestBody.description: Intent + profile fields (name, title) + optional tenant name / invitation token

201.description: Account created. If `verified` and tenant resolved, includes session + ld-tenant / ld-division response headers

400.description: Invalid input or already-existing user

get.description: Returns public plan and pricing information without requiring authentication.
Returns all tenants the calling user is a member of. Used by the console to populate the tenant switcher. With API key auth this is scoped to the key's tenant.

401.description: No active session or API key

post.description: Creates a new tenant with the caller as owner. Optionally provisions a default division in the same request. The new ids are returned in `ld-tenant` and `ld-division` response headers. Subject to per-user `owned_tenants` limit. Session-only: API keys are tenant-scoped and cannot create new tenants.

requestBody.description: Name, description, email, protected, optional initial division

201.description: Tenant created. The new tenant ID is returned in the ld-tenant header

400.description: Invalid name / email / division settings or owned-tenants limit reached

get.description: Returns tenant details: status, subscription plan + features, billing email, custom email domain. The caller must be a member of the tenant.

403.description: Not a member of the tenant

put.description: Partial update of tenant attributes (name, description, email, protected). Owner-only.

requestBody.description: Partial update. Null or missing fields are unchanged

400.description: Invalid field value

delete.description: Permanently deletes the tenant and all child resources (divisions, environments, deployments will be torn down). Requires a resource confirmation code (obtain via PUT /tenants/{tenant_id}/request_code with action `delete_tenant`). Owner-only. Outstanding deployments and billing must be settled first. Session-only: API keys are tenant-scoped and cannot delete tenants.

400.description: Active deployments or unpaid invoices exist, or missing/invalid code

get.description: Returns the tenant's API keys. Metadata only - the `token` secret is never included in list responses.

post.description: Creates a tenant-scoped API key. Provide `role_id` to reuse an existing role, or `permissions` to mint a dedicated single-purpose role automatically. The returned `token` is shown ONCE - store it immediately, it cannot be retrieved again.

requestBody.description: Name, expiry (max 365 days), role_id OR inline permissions, optional IP allowlist

201.description: API key created. `token` returned once and never again

400.description: Invalid name, expiry beyond 365 days, or both role_id and permissions provided

409.description: Name already used in this tenant or limit reached

get.description: Returns metadata about the API key making this call: role, permissions, expiry, IP allowlist. Lets an autonomous agent introspect its own authority before attempting actions.

200.description: Calling API key context and permissions

401.description: Caller is not authenticated via API key

get.description: Returns full metadata for an API key: role, permission tree, IP allowlist. Token secret is never returned.

delete.description: Immediately revokes the API key. Subsequent requests using its token will return 401. In-flight requests complete normally. Cannot be undone - create a new key if you need to restore access.

put.description: Updates only the security policy (IP validation + allowed_ips list). Role and permissions cannot be changed - delete and recreate the key instead, which keeps audit trails clean.

requestBody.description: Toggle validate_ip and/or replace allowed_ips list

400.description: Invalid CIDR, or validate_ip=true with empty allowed_ips

get.description: Returns the tenant billing recipient profile used for invoicing.

put.description: Updates the tenant billing recipient profile used for invoicing.

requestBody.description: Billing recipient fields such as company, address, tax ID, email, and phone

get.description: Returns paged customer invoices for the tenant.
Returns full invoice details for one tenant invoice.
Downloads the rendered PDF file for one invoice.

post.description: Creates a Stripe setup intent so the client can collect and attach a payment method for the tenant.

get.description: Returns the tenant's current payment provider and stored payment method metadata.

delete.description: Detaches the current payment method for the tenant.

get.description: Returns paged deployment billing reports for a tenant.
Returns one deployment billing report with detailed usage and pricing breakdown.
Returns the tenant's registered cloud accounts.

post.description: Registers an external cloud provider account (AWS or GCP) for BYOC deployments, VPC peering, and PrivateLink. Stores credentials and network metadata under the tenant.

requestBody.description: Provider, account ID, region, provider-specific settings

400.description: Invalid provider or settings

409.description: Name already used in this tenant

get.description: Returns full details of a registered cloud account, including provider-specific settings.

put.description: Updates name, region, settings, or remarks. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Account provider type is immutable.

requestBody.description: Partial update. Null or missing fields are unchanged

400.description: Invalid settings

delete.description: Removes a registered cloud account. Fails if any deployments, VPC peerings, or PrivateLink endpoints still reference it.

400.description: Account still referenced by deployments or network resources

get.description: Returns the cloud providers (AWS, GCP) available for deployments in this tenant.
Returns the regions available for deployment in the selected cloud provider.
Returns the cluster sizes/kinds (instance types + node counts) available for deployment in the selected cloud + region.

200.description: Cluster kinds available in the region

get.description: Returns the storage classes (local, EBS, persistent disk) available for deployment in the selected cloud + region.

200.description: Storage options available in the region

get.description: Returns the deployment tiers (e.g. starter, standard, enterprise) available for the selected cloud + region.

200.description: Tier options available in the region

get.description: Returns the tenant's organizational policy: join policy, invitation rules, and email-domain claim status.

403.description: Not a member of the tenant

put.description: Updates organizational policy: join_policy (open / invite_only / domain_match), whether external invitations are allowed, and whether invitations must come from the claimed email domain.

requestBody.description: Join policy + invitation policies

get.description: Returns the tenant's divisions visible to the caller. Permission-filtered: only divisions where the calling role has at least read access are included.

post.description: Creates a division inside the tenant. `protected` divisions require a resource confirmation code on delete. The new division ID is returned in the `ld-division` response header.

requestBody.description: Name (required), description, billing email, protected flag

201.description: Division created. The new division ID is returned in the ld-division header

400.description: Invalid name / description / email or tenant divisions limit reached

get.description: Returns division details including description, billing email, and whether a payment method is attached. Divisions are tenant subunits used for billing isolation and environment grouping.

put.description: Updates division attributes. All fields are optional - omitted fields are unchanged. Toggling `protected` from false to true requires the division to be in a known-good state.

requestBody.description: Partial update. Null or missing fields are unchanged

400.description: Invalid field value

delete.description: Deletes the division. Protected divisions require a resource code (obtain via PUT /tenants/{tenant_id}/request_code with action `delete_division`). The division must be empty of environments/deployments first.

400.description: Division still contains environments / deployments, or missing code on protected division

post.description: Creates or reuses an environment and schedules a starter deployment for the tenant/division.

requestBody.description: Starter deployment request

202.description: Starter deployment scheduled. The ld-environment and ld-deployment headers are set

get.description: Returns the division's environments visible to the caller. Permission-filtered.

post.description: Creates an environment in the division. Environments are the natural API key scope unit: scope a key to a single environment to bound an agent's blast radius. New id returned in the `ld-environment` response header.

requestBody.description: Name, optional description, protected flag

201.description: Environment created. The new environment ID is returned in the ld-environment header

400.description: Invalid name / description or environments limit reached

409.description: Name already used in this division

get.description: Returns environment details including description and deployment count. Environments group deployments within a division and are the smallest unit for fine-grained API key scoping.

put.description: Partial update of environment attributes. Omitted fields are unchanged.

requestBody.description: Partial update. Null or missing fields are unchanged

400.description: Invalid field value

delete.description: Deletes the environment. Must be empty of deployments first. Protected environments require a resource code (obtain via PUT /tenants/{tenant_id}/request_code with action `delete_environment`).

400.description: Environment contains deployments or missing code on protected env

get.description: Returns the environment's deployments visible to the caller. Permission-filtered.

post.description: Schedules a BYOC deployment into the caller's AWS or GCP account. Cloud-specific identity and network settings are included in the request body.

requestBody.description: BYOC deployment spec

202.description: BYOC deployment scheduled. The ld-environment and ld-deployment headers are set

post.description: Returns cloud-specific onboarding instructions and values required before creating a BYOC deployment.

requestBody.description: Target cloud and region

400.description: Invalid cloud or region

post.description: Creates a LaserData-managed deployment inside an existing environment. Returns accepted immediately. Provisioning continues asynchronously.

requestBody.description: Managed deployment spec

202.description: Deployment scheduled. The ld-environment and ld-deployment headers are set

post.description: Returns a rough monthly cost estimate for a hypothetical deployment based on cloud, region, tier, storage, throughput, and topology. The figure is an estimate only - it is computed from public list pricing without tenant-specific discounts or final billing rules, and may differ from what is actually invoiced. Free tier always returns zero. The endpoint never creates a deployment.

requestBody.description: Deployment shape to estimate

400.description: Invalid request body

get.description: Returns deployment details including cluster size, region, runtime status, and storage configuration. The `supervisor_url` field is the base URL of the supervisor API that owns this deployment's lifecycle (status, configuration, telemetry, restart, upgrade, node operations) - direct subsequent management calls there. Example: `https://supervisor-aws-us.laserdata.cloud`.

put.description: Updates mutable deployment metadata such as protection flag and description.

requestBody.description: Deployment metadata update

delete.description: Schedules deletion of the deployment. Protected deployments require a resource code (obtain via PUT /tenants/{tenant_id}/request_code with action `delete_deployment`).

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Resource confirmation code for protected deployments

400.description: Missing or invalid code on protected deployment

get.description: Returns the connector catalog with availability and activation status for the deployment. Filter by `type` query parameter (`source` or `sink`).

post.description: Activates a connector instance on the deployment. The instance starts in Pending status and transitions to Active once nodes process the task. Poll the connector list to confirm readiness.

requestBody.description: Connector type + provider-specific config

400.description: Invalid or unsupported connector config

post.description: Schedules horizontal scaling for a deployment by adding nodes.

requestBody.description: Nodes to add by runtime group

put.description: Updates telemetry retention policy for the deployment.

requestBody.description: Retention settings

put.description: Sets or clears the monthly spend cap for the deployment.

requestBody.description: Optional monthly spend limit

post.description: Schedules a deployment upgrade such as tier or storage changes.

requestBody.description: Requested deployment upgrade

get.description: Aggregate counters for the division: environments + deployments totals. Cheap projection for dashboards and agent context priming.
Returns outstanding invitations sent from this tenant (pending / accepted / rejected). Filter via the underlying query params.

post.description: Sends an invitation email. If the email already belongs to a registered user, the invitation appears in their /account/invitations list. Otherwise the invitee receives a sign-up link. Subject to tenant invitation policy (open / domain_only / block_external).

requestBody.description: Email (required) + optional division scope + optional role ids

400.description: Invalid email, violates tenant invitation policy, already invited, or already a member

delete.description: Revokes an outstanding invitation. The invitee can no longer accept it. Use this to revoke before expiry if circumstances change.

get.description: Returns paginated tenant members with role + permission summary per member. Filter by active status via the `active` query parameter.
Returns every tenant member at once with minimal fields (id, email, name). Use for member picker UIs. For tenants with many members, prefer the paginated GET /tenants/{id}/members.
Returns the full catalog of permissions available in this tenant, grouped by scope (tenant / division / environment). Use to populate role-permission selectors.

put.description: Toggle active status or replace the member's role assignment. Setting `active = false` keeps the membership record but blocks sign-in to the tenant. Setting `roles` replaces the full set atomically.

requestBody.description: Partial update. Null or missing fields are unchanged

400.description: Cannot update self or tenant owner

delete.description: Removes the member's tenant membership. Cannot remove the tenant owner or yourself - use DELETE /tenants/{tenant_id}/membership for self-removal.

400.description: Cannot delete yourself or the tenant owner

delete.description: Removes the current user's membership from this tenant. The tenant owner cannot leave - they must transfer ownership or delete the tenant first. Session-only: API keys are tenant-scoped and cannot leave tenants.

400.description: Caller is the tenant owner and cannot leave

404.description: Not a member of this tenant

put.description: Mints a one-time confirmation code emailed to the caller. Required for irreversible operations on `protected` resources (delete_tenant, delete_division, delete_environment, delete_deployment). The code is included on the subsequent DELETE call as a query parameter.

requestBody.description: Which destructive action the code authorizes

204.description: Code requested. Sent by email to the caller

403.description: Insufficient permissions for the requested action

get.description: Returns the tenant's roles. System roles (Owner, Admin, Member, Viewer) plus any custom roles. Filter by `kind` to separate system from custom.

post.description: Creates a custom role with a permission tree spanning tenant + division + environment scopes. New id returned in `ld-role` header. System roles cannot be created via this API.

requestBody.description: Name + permissions tree. System role kind is rejected - all created roles are Custom.

201.description: Role created. The new role ID is returned in the ld-role header

400.description: Invalid name, invalid permissions tree, or roles limit reached

get.description: Returns role details including full permission tree (tenant + division + environment scopes).

put.description: Updates a custom role's name or permissions tree. System roles cannot be modified.

requestBody.description: Partial update. Null or missing fields are unchanged

400.description: Invalid name or permissions

403.description: Cannot modify system role or insufficient permissions

delete.description: Deletes a custom role. Members assigned to it lose its permissions. System roles cannot be deleted.

403.description: Cannot delete system role or insufficient permissions

get.description: Returns the users currently assigned to this role.

put.description: Adds existing members to the role. Members keep any other roles they already have.

requestBody.description: List of member user ids to add to the role

400.description: Empty members list, members not in tenant, or cannot assign self

put.description: Removes members from the role. They keep their other role assignments and tenant membership.

requestBody.description: List of member user ids to remove from the role

400.description: Empty members list or cannot revoke from self

get.description: Returns the entire tenant resource hierarchy as a nested tree: divisions -> environments -> deployments. Single call to prime an agent's context about everything in the tenant. Permission-filtered, hidden divisions and environments are omitted. Each deployment's `supervisor_url` points to the supervisor API that owns its lifecycle (status, configuration, telemetry, restart, upgrade, node operations).

403.description: Not a member of the tenant

get.description: Aggregate counters for the tenant: total divisions, environments, deployments. Cheap projection for dashboards.

403.description: Not a member of the tenant

instance.description: RFC 7807 instance URI identifying the specific occurrence; mirrors the `ld-request` header value.

reason.description: RFC 7807 detail string. Long-form human explanation of this occurrence.

status.description: Mirror of HTTP status code. Agents can branch on the body without re-reading the response status.

title.description: RFC 7807 short, human-readable title for the error class.

type.description: RFC 7807 type URI identifying the error class. `about:blank` when no type is registered.

GcpProjectId.description:
A validated GCP project ID.

GCP project IDs must follow these rules:
- 6–30 characters
- Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only
- Starts with a lowercase letter
- Does not end with a hyphen

GcpServiceAccountEmail.description:
A validated GCP service account email address.

GCP service account emails follow the format:
  `{name}@{project}.iam.gserviceaccount.com`

Validation rules:
- Must contain exactly one `@`
- Must end with `.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
- Must not contain path-traversal or control characters (`/`, `\`, `:`)
- The local part (before `@`) must be non-empty

This newtype prevents URL injection when the email is interpolated into
the IAM Credentials API impersonation endpoint.

ld_api_key.name: ld-api-key
ld_api_key.description: Tenant API key issued via POST /tenants/{tenant_id}/api_keys. Sent in the ld-api-key request header. Scoped to tenant-level operations only. Cannot be used on user-scope endpoints (`/account/*`) or for tenant creation.

session_cookie.name: session
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /account/sign_in. Required for user-scope endpoints and tenant creation. Mutating endpoints additionally require the X-CSRF-Token header echoed from the sign-in response.
